66: def _compute_lfric_inner_products(prog, scalars, field_sums, sum_sym):
67:     '''
68:     Adds PSyIR to a supplied Routine to compute the sum of the inner products
69:     of the supplied scalars and fields.
70: 
71:     :param prog: the Routine to which to add PSyIR.
72:     :type prog: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Routine`
73:     :param scalars: list of pairs of scalars to multiply and sum.
74:     :type scalars: List[Tuple[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`,
75:                               :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`]]
76:     :param field_sums: the results of all of the inner products of the \
77:                        various field arguments.
78:     :type field_sums: List[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`]
79:     :param sum_sym: the symbol into which to accumulate the final sum.
80:     :type sum_sym: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`
81: 
82:     '''
83:     table = prog.symbol_table
84:     idef_sym = table.add_lfric_precision_symbol("i_def")
85:     idef_type = ScalarType(ScalarType.Intrinsic.REAL, idef_sym)
86: 
87:     # Initialise the sum to zero: sum = 0.0
88:     prog.addchild(Assignment.create(Reference(sum_sym),
89:                                     Literal("0.0", sum_sym.datatype)))
90:     for scalar in scalars:
91:         # Compute the product of the pair of scalars: scalar[0]*scalar[1]
92:         # (unless they are boolean).
93:         if scalar[0].datatype.intrinsic == ScalarType.Intrinsic.BOOLEAN:
94:             continue
95:         prod = BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.MUL,
96:                                       Reference(scalar[0]),
97:                                       Reference(scalar[1]))
98:         # Add this product to the sum:
99:         #     sum = sum + scalar[0]*scalar[1]
100:         prog.addchild(
101:                 Assignment.create(
102:                     Reference(sum_sym),
103:                     BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD,
104:                                            Reference(sum_sym), prod)))
105:     for sym in field_sums:
106:         if sym.is_scalar:
107:             # Add this result of a field inner product to the sum:
108:             #     sum = sum + field_sum
109:             prog.addchild(
110:                     Assignment.create(
111:                         Reference(sum_sym),
112:                         BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD,
113:                                                Reference(sum_sym),
114:                                                Reference(sym))))
115:         else:
116:             # For a field vector we have an array of inner-product values that
117:             # must be summed.
118:             for dim in range(int(sym.datatype.shape[0].lower.value),
119:                              int(sym.datatype.shape[0].upper.value)+1):
120:                 # sum = sum + field_sum(dim)
121:                 add_op = BinaryOperation.create(
122:                     BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD,
123:                     Reference(sum_sym),
124:                     ArrayReference.create(sym,
125:                                           [Literal(str(dim), idef_type)]))
126:                 prog.addchild(Assignment.create(Reference(sum_sym), add_op))
127:

129: def _compute_field_inner_products(routine, field_pairs):
130:     '''
131:     Constructs the assignments and kernel functors needed to compute the
132:     inner products of the supplied list of fields.
133: 
134:     :param routine: the routine to which to add the assignments.
135:     :type routine: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Routine`
136:     :param field_pairs: the pairs of fields for which we need to compute the \
137:                         inner products.
138:     :type field_pairs: List[ \
139:                Tuple[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`, \
140:                      :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`]]
141: 
142:     :returns: the symbols containing the inner products and the list of \
143:               kernel functors that computes them.
144:     :rtype: Tuple[List[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`], \
145:               List[:py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.algorithm.KernelFunctor`]]
146: 
147:     :raises TypeError: if any of the supplied symbols are not DataSymbols.
148:     :raises InternalError: if any of the supplied pairs of symbols do not \
149:                            have matching types.
150:     :raises InternalError: if any of the supplied symbols are not of the \
151:                            correct type for an LFRic field.
152: 
153:     '''
154:     # pylint: disable=too-many-branches, too-many-locals
155:     table = routine.symbol_table
156:     rdef_sym = table.add_lfric_precision_symbol("r_def")
157:     rdef_type = ScalarType(ScalarType.Intrinsic.REAL, rdef_sym)
158:     idef_sym = table.add_lfric_precision_symbol("i_def")
159:     idef_type = ScalarType(ScalarType.Intrinsic.REAL, idef_sym)
160: 
161:     builtin_factory = LFRicBuiltinFunctorFactory.get()
162: 
163:     field_ip_symbols = []
164:     kernel_list = []
165:     for sym1, sym2 in field_pairs:
166: 
167:         if not (isinstance(sym1, DataSymbol) and isinstance(sym2, DataSymbol)):
168:             raise TypeError(
169:                 f"Each pair of fields/field-vectors must be supplied as "
170:                 f"DataSymbols but got: {type(sym1)}, {type(sym2)}")
171: 
172:         if sym1.datatype != sym2.datatype:
173:             raise InternalError(
174:                 f"Cannot compute the inner product of fields '{sym1.name}' "
175:                 f"and '{sym2.name}' because they are of different types: "
176:                 f"{sym1.datatype} and {sym2.datatype}")
177: 
178:         if sym1 is sym2:
179:             inner_prod_name = f"{sym1.name}_inner_prod"
180:         else:
181:             inner_prod_name = f"{sym1.name}_{sym2.name}_inner_prod"

36: ''' Provides various utilities in support of the PSyAD adjoint
37:     functionality. '''
38: 
39: from psyclone.errors import InternalError
40: from psyclone.psyir.frontend.fortran import FortranReader
41: from psyclone.psyir.nodes import (IntrinsicCall, BinaryOperation,
42:                                   Reference, Assignment, IfBlock,
43:                                   Container, FileContainer, Node)
44: from psyclone.psyir.symbols import DataSymbol
45: 
46: 
47: #: The prefix we will prepend to routine, container and metadata
48: #: names when generating the adjoint. If the original name contains
49: #: the tl prefix, then this is removed.
50: ADJOINT_NAME_PREFIX = "adj_"
51: TL_NAME_PREFIX = "tl_"
52: #: The tolerance applied to the comparison of the inner product values in
53: #: the generated test-harness code.
54: #: TODO #1346 this tolerance should be user configurable.
55: INNER_PRODUCT_TOLERANCE = 1500.0
56:

58: def create_adjoint_name(tl_name):
59:     '''Create an adjoint name from the supplied tangent linear name. This
60:     is done by stripping the TL_NAME_PREFIX from the name if it exists
61:     and then adding the ADJOINT_NAME_PREFIX. The adjoint name is also
62:     lower-cased.
63: 
64:     :param str: the tangent-linear name.
65: 
66:     :returns: the adjoint name.
67:     :rtype: str
68: 
69:     '''
70:     adj_name = tl_name.lower()
71:     if adj_name.startswith(TL_NAME_PREFIX):
72:         adj_name = adj_name[len(TL_NAME_PREFIX):]
73:     return ADJOINT_NAME_PREFIX + adj_name
74:

76: def create_real_comparison(sym_table, kernel, var1, var2):
77:     '''
78:     Creates PSyIR that checks the values held by Symbols var1 and var2 for
79:     equality, allowing for machine precision.
80: 
81:     :param sym_table: the SymbolTable in which to put new Symbols.
82:     :type sym_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
83:     :param kernel: the routine for which this adjoint test is being performed.
84:     :type kernel: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Routine`
85:     :param var1: the symbol holding the first value for the comparison.
86:     :type var1: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`
87:     :param var2: the symbol holding the second value for the comparison.
88:     :type var2: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataSymbol`
89: 
90:     :returns: the PSyIR nodes that perform the check.
91:     :rtype: list of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
92: 
93:     '''
94:     freader = FortranReader()
95:     statements = []
96:     mtol = sym_table.new_symbol("MachineTol", symbol_type=DataSymbol,
97:                                 datatype=var1.datatype)
98:     rel_diff = sym_table.new_symbol("relative_diff", symbol_type=DataSymbol,
99:                                     datatype=var1.datatype)
100:     overall_tol = sym_table.new_symbol("overall_tolerance",
101:                                        symbol_type=DataSymbol,
102:                                        datatype=var1.datatype,
103:                                        is_constant=True,
104:                                        initial_value=INNER_PRODUCT_TOLERANCE)
105:     assign = freader.psyir_from_statement(
106:         f"MachineTol = SPACING ( MAX( ABS({var1.name}), ABS({var2.name}) ) )",
107:         sym_table)
108:     statements.append(assign)
109:     statements[-1].preceding_comment = (
110:         "Test the inner-product values for equality, allowing for the "
111:         "precision of the active variables")
112:     sub_op = BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.SUB,
113:                                     Reference(var1), Reference(var2))
114:     abs_op = IntrinsicCall.create(IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.ABS, [sub_op])
115:     div_op = BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.DIV,
116:                                     abs_op, Reference(mtol))
117:     statements.append(Assignment.create(Reference(rel_diff), div_op))
118: 
119:     # TODO #1345 make this code language agnostic.
120:     write1 = freader.psyir_from_statement(
121:         f"write(*,*) 'Test of adjoint of ''{kernel.name}'' PASSED: ', "
122:         f"{var1.name}, {var2.name}, {rel_diff.name}", sym_table)
123:     write2 = freader.psyir_from_statement(
124:         f"write(*,*) 'Test of adjoint of ''{kernel.name}'' FAILED: ', "
125:         f"{var1.name}, {var2.name}, {rel_diff.name}", sym_table)
126: 
127:     statements.append(
128:         IfBlock.create(BinaryOperation.create(BinaryOperation.Operator.LT,
129:                                               Reference(rel_diff),
130:                                               Reference(overall_tol)),
131:                        [write1], [write2]))
132: 
133:     return statements
134: 
135: 
136: def find_container(psyir):
137:     ''' Finds the first Container in the supplied PSyIR that is not a
138:     FileContainer. Also validates that the PSyIR contains at most one
139:     FileContainer which, if present, contains a Container.
140: 
141:     :param psyir: the PSyIR to search for a Container.
142:     :type psyir: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
143: 
144:     :returns: the first Container that is not a FileContainer or None if \
145:               there is none.
146:     :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Container` or NoneType
147: 
148:     :raises InternalError: if there are two Containers and the second is a \
149:                            FileContainer.
150:     :raises NotImplementedError: if there are two Containers and the first is \
151:                                  not a FileContainer.
152:     :raises NotImplementedError: if there are more than two Containers.
153: 
154:     '''
155:     if not isinstance(psyir, Node):
156:         raise TypeError(
157:             f"Expected a PSyIR Node but got '{type(psyir).__name__}'")
158: 
159:     containers = psyir.walk(Container)
160:     if not containers:
161:         return None
162: 
163:     if len(containers) == 1:
164:         if isinstance(containers[0], FileContainer):
165:             return None
166:         return containers[0]
167: 
168:     if len(containers) == 2:
169:         if isinstance(containers[1], FileContainer):
170:             raise InternalError(
171:                 "The supplied PSyIR contains two Containers but the innermost "
172:                 "is a FileContainer. This should not be possible.")
173:         if not isinstance(containers[0], FileContainer):
174:             raise NotImplementedError(
175:                 "The supplied PSyIR contains two Containers and the outermost "
176:                 "one is not a FileContainer. This is not supported.")
177:         return containers[1]
178: 
179:     raise NotImplementedError("The supplied PSyIR contains more than two "
180:                               "Containers. This is not supported.")
181: 
182: 
183: __all__ = ["create_adjoint_name", "create_real_comparison", "find_container"]
